text:
I’ve seen big shifts before. The internet 🌐 redefined software roles, and I believe AI is now driving the next transformation. 🤖

In the early days, software teams were filled with roles—requirements engineers, project managers, testers, UX designers, architects, and more. Over time, competition and the need for speed pushed companies to simplify. What emerged were two main roles most teams still rely on today:

➡️ Product Manager 🧑‍💼
➡️ Software Engineer 🧑‍💻

My vision is that AI will compress roles again before new ones grow out of it. From what I see, two core roles are on the horizon:

1️⃣ Product Engineer
A fusion of Product and Engineering. This role guides AI, writes code when needed, defines requirements, and carries features all the way from business problem to delivery. A full-spectrum owner. 💪

2️⃣ AI Ops
A unification of DevOps, Data Science, and Data Engineering. They’ll run MCP gateways, manage pipelines, connect data, and keep AI models and systems operating at scale. 🛠️

The reason is clear: businesses demand speed and flexibility. Fewer, broader roles make organizations faster, simpler, and more adaptable.

My vision is that, just like the internet era reshaped our work, AI will reorganize roles and responsibilities until they align with the new drivers. 🔄

I see this change already forming. Do you share this vision in your organization? 🤔
